publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The effect of solvent on the carrier transport in poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(4-styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) was studied by the combination of THz time-domain transmission spectroscopy (0.1-3 THz) and the broadband reflectance spectroscopy (4-800 THz). While the broadband reflectance showed a plasma edge in the near infrared, the frequency dependence of the THz conductivity of PEDOT:PSS indicated the weakly localized carrier behavior. The simultaneous fitting of both spectra by the localization modified Drude model allowed us to conclude that the significant increase of conductivity by adding ethylene glycol was quantitatively explained by the improvement of the carrier mobility in the PEDOT/PSS.

articleTitle: Thickness and substrate dependence of THz modulation efficiency in organic/inorganic semiconductor structures
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report on the thickness dependence of THz modulation efficiency in an organic phthalocyanine (CuPc) film on a Si wafer. The modulation efficiency is also associated with the inorganic semiconductor substrate. This finding confirms that the THz modulation is caused by the injected carriers, excited by optical excitation, into the CuPc film.

articleTitle: Frontend for a 2.5-THz heterodyne spectrometer without liquid cryogen
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: As part of a study for a second generation heterodyne spectrometer on SOFIA we are developing a 2.5-THz frontend which is implemented in a pulse-tube cooler. It consists of a quantum-cascade laser as local oscillator and a phonon-cooled NbN hot electron bolometric mixer. Frequency stabilization to below 300 kHz full width at half maximum is achieved by locking to a molecular absorption line. We will present the design and performance of the frontend and discuss the prospects for an application on board of SOFIA.

articleTitle: Study on the beam-wave interaction in the rectangular Cerenkov maser with a sheet electron beam
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A linear theory of a rectangular Cerenkov maser (RCM) with a sheet electron beam is developed by using Borgnis function method and field-match method. Based on a 3-D beam-wave interaction model proposed in this paper, the TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> mode dispersion equation and its analytical solution are derived for the RCM. Through numerical calculations, the effect of the beam thickness, current density and beam-grating gap on the linear growth rate is analyzed.

articleTitle: Concepts of terahertz and infrared devices based on graphene structures
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We overview novel concepts of terahertz and infrared interband detectors and lasers based on single- and multiple-graphene layer structures and discuss the features of their operation and feasibility of realization.

articleTitle: Terahertz field induced second harmonic generation in biomolecules
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report the THz field-induced-second-harmonic generation in various biomolecules including amino acids, proteins and sugars. The THz field induced optical second harmonic (SH) signal depends on the strength of THz beam and on the relative polarizations of optical and THz beam. The THz waveform is coherently retrieved from the time dependent SH signal.

articleTitle: Photoconductive THz generation at 1.5 μm excitation in InGaAs/InAlAs structures with separated photoconductive and trapping layers
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present first results on photoconductive switches based on MBE grown InGaAs/InAlAs multi-nanolayer structures with separated trapping and photoconductive layers, the later exhibiting high carrier mobility. The high mobility significantly increases the optical power-to-THz conversion efficiency, while the emitted THz bandwidth exceeds 3 THz.

articleTitle: High-order PIC simulations of microwave sources
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A highly parallelized 3D code, based on the Particle-In-Cell approach is used for self-consistent simulations of highly energetic microwave sources (gyrotron resonator and launcher) for fusion plasma heating. We present results for some isolated components of TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0, 3</sub> and the TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22, 6</sub> gyrotron.

articleTitle: Time-of-flight model for the extraordinary optical transmission through two dimensional aperture arrays
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A qualitative model describing the extraordinary optical transmission of THz radiation through periodic subwavelength two dimensional aperture arrays is presented. Extensive THz-TDS measurements support this model, where the combined effects of aperture shape, area, alignment and aspect ratio have been systematically investigated.

articleTitle: Far-field THz radiation pattern from photoconductive emitters on different substrates
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present measured terahertz radiation patterns from antennas made of low temperature grown gallium arsenide on semi-insulating gallium arsenide and low temperature grown gallium arsenide on high resistivity silicon. A strong dependence on the substrate used for the terahertz source can be shown.

articleTitle: Active terahertz metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present a series of novel THz metamaterials with designed active functionality, enabling dynamic tuning of the amplitude, frequency and polarization state of a THz wave.

articleTitle: Sampling geometries and resolution limits for compressive MMW and terahertz imaging
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Compressive measurement enables image formation from sparse and irregular arrays. In MMW and terahertz imaging, compressive measurement may lead to a preference for fewer but more complex transceivers over dense arrays of simple transceivers (e.g. conventional focal planes.).

articleTitle: Effects of spatial and temporal correlations of thermal fields in adsorbed molecule spectra
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Dynamics and absorption spectrum of molecular system interacting with thermal fluctuating fields generated by solid surfaces is studied.

articleTitle: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy of polyfluorene thin films
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report on electrical and optical properties of the 1 μm thick films of conjugated polymer poly[9,9-bis-(2-ethylhexyl)-9H-fluorene-2,7-diyl] (PFO) studied by terahertz (THz) spectroscopy. The spectra of characteristics of PFO films in the 0.2-3.0 THz frequency range can be well described by Lorentz oscillator model.

articleTitle: Monolithically integrated Bragg reflectors to improve on the emitted power from metal-metal THz quantum cascade lasers
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A metal-metal waveguide quantum cascade laser operating with a monolithically integrated Bragg reflector at ~ 2.9 THz is demonstrated. For a Bragg reflector spacing of λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>/4 emission is suppressed to below that of a conventional device architecture; while as the spacing approaches λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>/2 power increases. We observe an enhancement in emitted optical power by up to a factor of seven compared to a same sized device with no Bragg reflector.

articleTitle: Possibilities and advantages of coaxial gyrotron with two beams operation at high harmonic
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: One of the urgent problems in gyrotron development is to improve the operation frequency. In this paper, we investigate the possibilities of coaxial gyrotron with two beams (CGTB) operation at high harmonic. The results show that CGTB has potential advantages to operate at high harmonic.

articleTitle: Percolation-enhanced terahertz emission
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Emission of terahertz radiation is observed when semi-continuous ultrathin gold films near the percolation threshold are excited with femtosecond near-infrared laser pulses. Our experimental results suggest that the emission is through a percolation-enhanced second-order nonlinear optical rectification process.

articleTitle: The 500–700 GHz spectrometer with superconductive integrated receiver
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The nonstationary spectrometer of 500-700 GHz frequency range is presented. Radiation sources are harmonics obtained by semiconductor superlattice frequency multiplier. The receiving system is developed using a superconducting integrated receiver. The results of test measurements of NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> absorption lines (572 GHz) in exhaled air were presented.

articleTitle: Performance of THz fiber-scanning near-field microscopy to diagnose breast tumors
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Based on the statistics of 20 female patients, we demonstrate that the diagnostic sensitivity and specificity of the THz fiber-scanning near-field microscopy to examine breast tumor sections are all as high as 100%. It will be very useful for quick definition of the tumor margins during the surgical procedure such as breast-conserving surgery.

articleTitle: Terahertz radiation induced edge currents in graphene
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report on the observation of the terahertz radiation induced edge photogalvanic effect. The directed net electric current is generated in single layer graphene by the irradiation of the samples' edges with linearly or circularly polarized terahertz laser radiation at normal incidence. We show that the directed net electric current stems from the sample edges, which reduce locally the symmetry and result in an asymmetric scattering of carriers driven by the radiation field.

articleTitle: Transmission line performance and plans for the gyrotron complex on the DIII-D tokamak
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A major upgrade to the electron cyclotron heating complex on the DIII-D tokamak is underway. Two depressed collector gyrotrons are being added to the complex and the transmission lines are being upgraded. Transmission line efficiencies are being increased by reduction in the number of miter bends together with improved alignment resulting in improved mode purity.

articleTitle: Two-step projection iteration threshholding super resolution for passive millimeter imaging
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In Passive millimeter wave (PMMW) imaging, the low-pass effect of passive millimeter wave imaging system makes the space resolution very poor. In this paper, two-step projection iteration threshholding(twPIT) algorithm is proposed for the super-resolution process of passive millimeter wave imaging. This algorithm uses the sparse prior information and the non-negative finite value information of passive millimeter wave images, which can separate the noise from the signals in the iteration process. When the image noise is existed, our algorithm is also very effective and has good super-resolution performance.

articleTitle: Terahertz heterodyne detection and imaging with the InGaAs bow-tie diode
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Room-temperature detection and imaging at 0.591 THz with planar InGaAs bow-tie diodes are demonstrated in heterodyne scheme. The improvement of the dynamic range by heterodyning over direct power detection is estimated to be of about 40 dB using pixel read-out times relevant to real-time imaging conditions.

articleTitle: Terahertz radiation in a 3-mirror quasi-optical cavity
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Based on the Fabary-Parot cavity and subwavelength holes array, a 3-mirror quasi-optical cavity is presented and explored. The electron beam-wave interaction in this cavity is proposed and the results show that this interaction can reach an attractive value with reasonable current density of electron beam at THz regime.

articleTitle: Experimental characterization of Gold Nanoparticle suspensions at W band using a quasi-optical bench
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Nanoscale materials have some unique properties in THz band. Preliminary measurement has been conducted using a quasi-optical (QO) bench to explore the transmission characterization of Gold Nanoparticle (GNP) suspensions over the W-band (75-110 GHz).

articleTitle: Scattering estimation from spectral moments of THz-TDS signals
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Scattering poses a major challenge to the precise measurement of spectral parameters of various materials. In this paper, we propose a novel signal processing based method of estimating scattering loss of a medium without precise information of its granularity, refractive index, and density.

articleTitle: Fast control of depressed collector gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: High power gyrotrons for plasma heating utilize a single stage depressed collector potential in order to reduce the collector load and to recover a large fraction of the remaining energy of the spent electron beam. This operation mode requires two high voltage power supplies which usually possess different characteristics. In the case of RF modulation, both power supplies must nevertheless operate synchronously and with a certain timing. In addition, the power must be shut down instantaneously when the collector load exceeds a certain limit, e.g. due to a dropout of the RF output. This paper discusses the realization of the above functionality in a single FPGA and describes the implementation at the W7-X stellarator.

articleTitle: Ultrafast gain switching of THz quantum cascade lasers: Principle and applications
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Summary form only given. Ultrafast gain switching of THz quantum cascade lasers is demonstrated and applied to amplify sub-ps THz pulses as well as to initiate THz laser emission with a controlled phase. Impact on THz time domain spectroscopy and on future development for mode-locking will be discussed.

articleTitle: THz integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We will review our latest efforts at making THz integrated circuits, focusing mostly on integration of a Schottky diode into the core of a quantum cascade laser to create a heterodyne receiver. We will show its capability to detect external radiation and its ability to explore the behavior of the QCL itself.

articleTitle: Application of terahertz spectral imaging for the identification of osseous tissue
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present spectral imaging results of osseous tissues obtained through terahertz time-domain transmission spectroscopy. The spectral response of composite bone tissues was investigated using pixel by pixel frequency-domain analysis. Comparisons of the time-domain and spectral characteristics were used to distinguish between regions of differing cellular type, mixed composition, and thickness.

articleTitle: Squeezing radiation from quantum cascade lasers with leaky waves
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Several flat antennas consisting of a central slot surrounded by a metallic periodic structure are proposed to enhance the radiation of quantum cascade laser terahertz sources. A simulation study of the optimal profile for high gain and radiation efficiency is done. Prototypes are being fabricated.

articleTitle: Development of CW 16-element phased-array antenna for electron bernstein wave heating and current drive experiments in QUEST
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The 16-element phased-array antenna has been developed for the EBWH/CD experiments. The 2-D k-spectra could be controlled. The heat load and stress were analyzed to be moderate in the 200kW CW operation. The symmetrically 2-D narrow-field distributions were excited by the developed antenna, indicating its good applicability to the EBWH/CD experiments.

articleTitle: Investigation of MgB2 HEB mixer gain bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: THz mixers based on superconducting MgB<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> bolometers were fabricated by photolithography and Ar-ion beam milling on sapphire substrates. The mixer gain bandwidth of 3.4 GHz, 2.3 GHz and 1.3 GHz were measured for 10, 15 and 30 nm films respectively.

articleTitle: Time-dependent multi-mode nonlinear analysis of dual-frequency operation coaxial gyrotron with two electron beams
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The nonlinear coupling between modes and electron beams of the coaxial gyrotron with two electron beams (CGTB) has been investigated by means of the self-consistent time-dependent multi-mode nonlinear theory. The effects of the currents of two electron beams on the output power of two operating modes are discussed. It has been found that CGTB can operate at two different frequencies simultaneously with the given parameters and the peaks of the output power of two operating modes appear alternately with a certain period in dual-frequency operation. Compared with the coaxial gyrotron with one beam (CGOB) with the same parameters, the corresponding average output power of two operating modes in CGTB is enhanced due to the nonlinear coupling between operating modes and electron beams.

articleTitle: High power-long pulse transmission experiment of torus diamond window for ITER EC H&CD system
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A torus diamond window prototype for an ITER electron cyclotron heating and current drive (EC H&CD) system was fabricated based on the latest design. It was installed in the ITER relevant transmission line and high power-long pulse experiment was carried out. Transmission of 740kW-100sec and was performed. It was observed that the cooling water temperature was stabilized and significant low loss tangent, 5.54 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> was estimated. The results promise that our torus diamond window is feasible to high power-long pulse transmission.

articleTitle: Terahertz-wave induced near-infrared transparency in graphene
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We have succeeded to induce huge near-infrared transparency by intense terahertz-wave excitation with 200kV/cm in the electric field. Ballistic acceleration of carriers should take place under the strong electric field and result in non-thermal carrier distribution of electrons and holes, giving rise to absorption saturation.

articleTitle: Low-frequency spectra in hydrophobic environment studied by terahertz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Low-frequency spectrum of hydration water molecules around the hydrophobic probe in an aqueous solution has been obtained by using tetraalkylammonium cation as a probe and terahertz time-domain spectroscopy. The obtained spectrum of hydration water has intensity larger than that of ice and smaller than that of bulk water. This suggests that dynamics of hydration water molecules are partially restricted compared to those of bulk water.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic pulser for the investigation of cell membranes
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: An electron based radiation source is presented with the aim of irradiating cell membrane models and biological cell membranes. The peculiarity of the device is that it can simultaneously generate short electromagnetic pulses, in the millimeter wave range, and electrostatic pulses with the same time structure.

articleTitle: Resonant mode splitting due to the symmetry breaking in a coupled slit structure
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report on the splitting of the resonant transmission mode, due to the symmetry breaking of the structural shape, in a coupled slit structure. The finding demonstrates the important role of the shape symmetry in designing a plasmonic structure for high-efficiency transmission modulation and supports possibilities of developing new terahertz devices.

articleTitle: GaAs/Al0.15Ga0.85As terahertz quantum cascade lasers with double-phonon resonant depopulation operating up to 172 K
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report the design and performance of GaAs/Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.85</sub>As terahertz quantum cascade lasers with double-phonon resonant depopulation and a vertical lasing transition. Lasing at 3 THz was observed up to a heat-sink temperature of 172 K.

articleTitle: Mixing THz quantum cascade lasers with an optical frequency comb
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A new scheme for coherent detection of a laser electric field has been demonstrated by stabilizing the emission frequency of a THz quantum cascade laser (QCL) on a harmonic of the repetition rate of a fs-fiber laser. This scheme has permitted to measure the pulses (10ps long) of a QCL that operates mode-locking, while the injected current is modulated close to its round trip frequency.

articleTitle: Extraordinary THz transmission in ring apertures
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We demonstrated extraordinary THz transmission through ring apertures on a metal film. Transmission of 60% was obtained with an aperture-to-area ratio of only 1.4%. We show that the high transmission can be suppressed by over 18 dB with a thin layer of free carriers in the silicon substrate underneath the metal film. This result suggests that CMOS-compatible terahertz switch can be built by controlling the carrier density near the aperture.

articleTitle: Nanoscale infrared spectroscopy with a thermal source: Nano-FTIR
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We demonstrate a FTIR system that allows for infrared-spectroscopic nano-imaging with a thermal source (nano-FTIR). Based on super-focusing of thermal radiation with an infrared antenna and strong signal enhancement using an asymmetric FTIR spectrometer, we improve the spatial resolution of conventional IR spectroscopy by 2 orders of magnitude.

articleTitle: Dependence of output power on slot antenna width in terahertz oscillating resonant tunneling diodes
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report on the dependence of output power on slot antenna width in resonant tunneling diodes (RTDs) with offset-fed slot antennas oscillating at ~500GHz. The output power was maximized at an optimized slot width through the impedance matching between the RTD and antenna. Theoretical calculation reasonably agreed with the experiment.

articleTitle: Study of two-dimensional periodic surface lattices for high-power mm and sub-mm wave Cherenkov devices
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Studies of a periodic surface lattice and a surface field oscillator based on such a lattice, producing radiation at high-GHz frequencies are presented. The scalability of the oscillator is discussed. The influence of the structure's parameters on the Cherenkov device's performance is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Leaky wave antennas based on transmission line metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: This paper reviews progress of development and applications of the leaky wave antennas (LWA) based on the transmission line metamaterial over the past several years.

articleTitle: Solutions for high sensitivity direct detection in submillimeter astronomy
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The sensitivity specifications for next generation submillimeter instruments for astronomy, astrophysics and cosmology are between 1 and 2 orders of magnitude better than state of the art instruments like Herschel PACS. We are studying new solutions using semiconducting bolometers in order to achieve the required performances. We show that with minimum changes compared to our existing technology, we obtain very good performances with detectors that are very similar to the ones used for PACS. We also show our plans to go beyond these values.

articleTitle: Continuous wave terahertz generation and coherent detection with dual-mode laser diode and InGaAs-based photomixers
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We demonstrate continuous wave (CW) THz generation with a compact dual-mode laser diode (DML) and InGaAs-based photomixers (PMs). By tuning the output wavelengths of the DML, we achieved THz tuning more than 1 THz. We detected THz output from PM emitter using coherent detection scheme.

articleTitle: Coherent terahertz radiation from TTF-TCNQ films irradiated with optical pulses
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We have observed coherent terahertz emission from TTF-TCNQ films excited by femtosecond laser pulses. The waveform consists of a weak pulse and damped oscillations with a frequency of 1.4 THz. The oscillations are considered to be radiation from optically excited coherent phonons.

articleTitle: On a tunable free-electron terahertz radiation source
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We propose a tunable free-electron terahertz diffraction radiation source making use of the special kind mechanism of diffraction radiation excited by electron beam coupling with the guided modes in a periodic structure [1,2]. The detailed theoretical investigation and digital simulation confirm the characteristics of the source. The terahertz diffraction radiation sources working around 1THz are proposed. Several promising ways of enhancing the radiation power and efficiency are also presented. Specially, the coherent diffraction radiation excited by pre-bunched electron beam is discussed theoretically and numerically. This mechanism of diffraction radiation may open a good opportunity to the vacuum electronic and bring attractive prospects to develop compact and tunable radiation sources in THz and higher frequency regime.

articleTitle: Numerical investigation of pseudospark discharged electron beam and propagation for W-band radiation
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A micro-klystron is one kind of compact device which can generate high power Terahertz radiation to meet the requirements of fast growing applications in Terahertz technology. The device needs a very thin electron beam with high energy to drive the beam-wave interaction. Pseudospark discharged electron beam has demonstrated its ability to provide a high current density in a small diameter (<; 0.2mm) for a W-Band micro-klystron.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous THz quantum cascade lasers: Broadband operation
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We demonstrate the operation of broadband heterogeneous terahertz quantum cascade lasers by carefully designing sub-stacks to align at the same field. Time domain spectroscopy measurements confirm that a flat gain spectrum is present and when incorporated into metal-metal waveguides we find broadband operation over 380 GHz when metal-metal ridges with non-vertical side-walls are used. In recent years there has been substantial growth in the research and development of terahertz (THz) sources. A THz source which has yet to reach its potential is the THz quantum cascade laser (QCL). These sources are based on intersubband transitions in quantum wells and are powerful, electrically driven and show operating temperatures of up to 187 K [1]. QCLs have intrinsically narrow gain spectrum, however for some applications a broad gain spectrum is very desirable. A THz QCL with a broad gain bandwidth could be used as an amplifier in THz TDS systems, as the gain medium in a tunable cavity [2] or in modelocking [3]. Broadband mid-IR QCLs make use of heterogeneous active regions [4], where two or more sub-stacks are combined into the same active region. We have recently shown two-colour lasing [5] from heterogeneous THz QCL designs and here we build on these results to produce devices which show broad band lasing. The heterogeneous two-colour design of reference [5] did not show the performance that was expected from the constituent sub-stacks; there was an elevated threshold for the higher frequency sub-stack and evidence from TDS measurements to suggest that a difference in alignment fields between the two sub-stacks was the cause. The solution to the issue of different electric fields is to use the flexibility of the QCL design to re-engineer the active regions to operate at the same electric field as well as the same current.

articleTitle: Multi detector terahertz beam profiling and imaging instrument
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A reconfigurable, all-reflective terahertz imager has been constructed, capable of 4096-pixel resolution in 20 seconds. The imager spans 0.09–0.90 THz in 5 bands, each represented by a 16-element detector array. Both, beam profiling and confocal imaging configurations have been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Design studies of a quasi-optical mode converter and output system for a second harmonic sub terahertz gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: This paper presents the design studies of the output coupling system of a 460 GHz, 50-100 W, CW, second harmonic gyrotron for medical spectroscopy. During this course, the design studies of an advanced dimpled-wall quasi optical launcher (QOL), non-linear taper and RF window will be carried out.

articleTitle: Large area self assembled tunable terahertz detector
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Recently compact frequency sensitive THz detection has been achieved using gated gratings on 2DEG structure. The method is based on the resonant absorption of the 2D plasmon dependence on tuning of carrier density by depletion gating. Here we demonstrate a method to improve detector sensitivity, tunability and remove polarization dependence through the development of a gated grid design. The requirement for imaging applications of device dimensions on the order of <;1 micron over a detector area of 4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, suggest that standard lithographic approaches will be too costly for large scale detector production. Here we realize the gated grid plasmonic structure on 2DEG material by using nanosphere self-assembly lithography.

articleTitle: Time-course analysis of tablet film-coating using terahertz pulsed imaging
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Quality attribute of tablet coating on a film-coating process was investigated by a terahertz pulsed imaging. The time-dependent change of intensities of reflex THz pulse and coating layer thicknesses were compared. The forming of coating layer was observed at 30 min after the process was started.

articleTitle: W-band two-dimensional periodic surface lattice for a surface field Cherenkov maser
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The design of an experiment to study a two-dimensional (2D) cylindrical lattice is presented. We illustrate the mode transformations inside the set-up and discuss planned experiments with the lattice. Investigations of a W-band periodic surface lattice are reported. This lattice is intended for use in a novel W-band surface field Cherenkov maser.

articleTitle: Fiber-connected terahertz time-domain spectroscopy system
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A flexible terahertz (THz)-time domain spectroscopy (TDS) system has been fabricated by using air guided photonic crystal fibers for 1.56 μm laser and a DAST crystal as an emitter. Using this system we could obtain reliable refractive index value n of Si in the frequency ranges from 0.2-2.8 THz.

articleTitle: Terahertz multichannel microfluidic sensor based on parallel-plate waveguide resonant cavities
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We demonstrate a terahertz multichannel microfluidic sensor based on a parallel-plate waveguide geometry with two independent integrated resonant cavities.

articleTitle: A 0.6 THz quasi-optical detector based on a room microbolometer
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: This paper reports the performance of a THz detector with a wide bandwidth based on Nb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> microbolometer operated at room temperature. This microbolometer integrated with a planar folded dipole antenna is fabricated on the high resistance Si substrates. The best attainable electrical responsibility of Nb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> microbolometer is about -600 V/W. A quasi-optical type detector based on this Nb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> microbolometer is constructed, and the result shows a good performance at a range of 0.6THz to 0.7THz.

articleTitle: Enhanced fano-like phonon resonance in heavily doped graphene
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A large enhancement in the intensity of in-plane optical phonon is observed in heavily doped graphene synthesized by chemical vapor deposition. This enhancement is due to the strong electron-phonon interaction in graphene.

articleTitle: Terahertz generation from DFG and TPG configurations
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Experimental results using two ways of Terahertz generation from difference frequency generation (DFG) in GaSe crystal and terahertz-wave parametric generator (TPG) in MgO doped LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> crystal are reported. High power and broad band frequency THz are generated from DFG, and obvious idler light and THz emission are observed from TPG configurations.

articleTitle: Novel fiber delivery of fs-laser pulses for THz generation without pre-chirping
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: By use of a novel ultrashort pulse fiber delivery laser pulses at 770 nm are delivered over 19 meters without pre-chirping. The fiber delivery module is described revealing its potential for remote distance THz applications.

articleTitle: Quantitative analysis of apertureless THz scanning near field optical microscopy based on an exact line dipole image method
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Summary form only given. We present the line dipole image method which is based on an analytic image theory. The probe tip on the sample substrate is approximated by a metallic sphere for calculation. Within the quasi-electrostatic limit, the exact image theory was iteratively applied to obtain the total induced dipole moment for the sample-substrate system. The experimental approach curves are explained. The measurements of approach curves on gold and silicon substrates were in excellent agreement with the line dipole calculations.

articleTitle: Fractal photoconductive THz emitters
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: New classes of photoconductive THz emitters based on Apollonian as well Sierpinski fractals and their complementary counter parts are presented. It is shown that for each fractal class the emitted THz radiation power increases as the fractal order is increased. It is shown that the self-similarity of plasmonic current present on the antenna surface results in superior performance compared to conventional bow-tie emitters.

articleTitle: Large strain-induced conductivity anisotropy in VO2 thin films, probed by THz spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We probe the temperature dependent far-infrared conductivity of highly strained (100) and (110) VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> thin films using THz Time Domain Spectroscopy. Large in-plane anisotropy is observed in both the metallic conductivity and the metal-insulator transition temperature.

articleTitle: Generation of MW radiation in a two-channel planar FEM with combined electrodynamic system
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Paper describes the first experiments on generation of 4-mm radiation in two-channel planar FEM with combined electrodynamic system carried out at the ELMI-device. The results of spectral and calorimetric measurements are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Frequency swept optical beat source for CW THz wave radiation
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We demonstrate a frequency swept optical beat source for high speed continuous wave THz generation. The range of the sweeping bandwidth is about 2.16 THz (17.3 nm). And we observe CW THz waveforms for several static optical beat sources using a fiber coupled CW THz measurement system in order to confirm the feasibility of our frequency swept optical beat source as a CW THz radiation source.

articleTitle: Near-field & far-field modelling of a sub-wavelength THz source
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The THz emission point on a nonlinear electro-optical crystal for generating broadband THz radiation is modeled as a radiating Gaussian aperture. With the wavelengths of the infrared pump beam being much smaller than the wavelength components of the generated THz pulse, a THz sub-wavelength radiating aperture with Gaussian profile is effectively created. This paper investigates this general modelling approach for focused THz radiation generation in electro-optical crystals. Different implementations are employed for the near- and far-field regime. While a numerical approach is required to characterize near-field intensity distributions, a semi-analytical model is sufficient for far-field considerations. The near-field study has ramifications in THz near-field focused beam techniques while far-field investigations elucidate the radiation pattern shape and hence the detectable SNR.

articleTitle: Nonlinear multimode interaction in a higher-order-mode cyclotron autoresonance maser
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A sub-terahertz (0.35 THz) CARM operating in a higher-order mode TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5,1</sub> is simulated, where nonlinear interaction of the operating mode with its neighboring modes TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5,2</sub>, TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5,1</sub>, and TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5,2</sub> are taken into account. Results show that the expected operating mode TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5,1</sub> with ultrahigh gain of 79 dB may be absolutely dominant, although all the neighboring modes grow simultaneously in the multimode-beam interaction process.

articleTitle: Single-, few-, and multi-cycle terahertz pulses generation from relativistic electrons
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report the generation and characterization of single-, few-, and multi-cycle terahertz pulses from relativistic electrons.

articleTitle: Total internal reflection Terahertz imaging
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present a new Terahertz imaging scheme based on total internal reflection that allows the study of aqueous samples while improving the longitudinal resolution. We were able to image a frog neuron using the spectral phase of the THz pulses using this technique.

articleTitle: Characterizing the impedance mismatch at the output of a terahertz parallel-plate waveguide
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We study the impedance mismatch for terahertz waves propagating in a parallel-plate waveguide via the TEM mode. The impedance mismatch is found to depend strongly on the plate separation.

articleTitle: Continuous wave terahertz transmission imaging through near-field aperture funnels
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report high throughput, continuous wave terahertz imaging using a near-field funnel aperture with adjustable output diameter. The frequency dependence of the output power and resolution immediately following the aperture are reported, as are the propagation and resolution characteristics as a function of distance from the aperture.

articleTitle: Heat transfer in beam optics analyzer
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Summary form only given. This paper will describe the new capability in BOA, the heat transfer integration with particle simulations. It will discuss implemented techniques to smooth the wall power density field generated by electron energy. It will explain the finite element method with adaptivity used to solve the heat equation, and provide numerical results to demonstrate the implementation.

articleTitle: Two-color nonlinear optical response of graphene with broken AB-symmetry
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We demonstrate that the bandgap opening in graphene induced by AB-sublattice symmetry breaking leads to a strong nonlinear optical response for frequencies well below the bandgap where linear response is strictly forbidden. Our result suggests that one type of graphene with such symmetry breaking, semihydrogenated graphene, can have a unique potential as a two-color nonlinear material in the terahertz photonics.

articleTitle: Large tuning range THz synthesiser by means of photomixing
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Photomixing is an attractive solution for high resolution spectroscopy, nevertheless it has suffered from a lack of frequency metrology to determine the line centre frequencies. Frequency combs can provide excellent metrology of lasers, hence we propose a photomixing source that is phase locked to a frequency comb to overcome this problem. The resulting instrument has an accuracy of Δν<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">THz</sub>/ν<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">THz</sub> = 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup>, a spectral purity in the order of 50 kHz and can be continuously tuned over 200 MHz.

articleTitle: Measurements of near terahertz conductivity of doped silicon using a high quality factor resonant cavity
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The conductivity of doped silicon is measured at 400 and 650 GHz. Measurements are performed using a high quality factor, semi-confocal resonant cavity. Data is presented which contradicts conventional theory (Drude model) and in agreement with a multiphysics computational model being developed at UW-Madison.

articleTitle: Near-field THz imaging of a split ring resonator matrix
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We investigated the spatiotemporal terahertz (THz) near-field distribution of a split ring resonators (SRR) matrix using a real-time THz microscope. The near-field THz imaging analysis on a large area revealed the photonic crystal properties of the SRR matrix. This technique may open a door for the development of high sensitivity biosensors.

articleTitle: Generation of THz radiation from a periodic electrostatic field via a relativistic ionization front
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We have a demonstrated the terahertz radiation by the interaction between a laser created relativistic underdense ionization front and a sinusoidal electrostatic field. The central frequencies of the radiation are observed to from 0.2 to 0.6 THz at the laser intensity at 3.5 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup> W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Lower frequency component is independent of the plasma frequency and higher one is attributed to the radiation from DARC structure.

articleTitle: Terahertz time domain spectroscopic evidence of charge-density-waves in Nd0.5Sr0.5MnO3 thin films
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Terahertz time domain spectroscopy was employed to explore the low-energy dynamics in the half-doped Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sub>Sr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sub>MnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (100) films. We have observed evolution of a peak structure in conductivity at around ~4 meV which suggests the existence of charge-density waves.

articleTitle: Design of a higher-order TM-mode coaxial Bragg resonator
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A coaxial Bragg resonator for a cyclotron auto-resonance maser (CARM) oscillator operating in the TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6, 2</sub> mode at frequency of 0.35 THz, is designed and analyzed. Numerical simulation shows that the coaxial Bragg resonator can be used to construct a THz high order TM-mode CARM oscillator.

articleTitle: Lifetime analysis of photoconductive THz emitters
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The durability of photoconductive Terahertz emitters significantly depends on bias voltage and/or optical power. We analyze the optimum operation conditions of photomixers for long-term performance and link the accessible signal-to-noise ratio to the photomixer lifetime via an Arrhenius analysis.

articleTitle: The free-electron laser as a tool for time-resolved, nonlinear, and near-field spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present three examples of infrared spectroscopic investigations of semiconductors: exciton dressed states in quantum wells, pump-probe measurements on graphene, and near-field spectroscopy of buried quantum dots.

articleTitle: Carbon nanotube arrays for absolute IR and THz radiometry
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We have assembled and evaluated a novel electrically calibrated thermopile having an array of 1.5 mm long multiwalled carbon nanotubes as the radiation absorber. We find very low reflectance at the 390 μm laser wavelength and excellent agreement between optical and electrical measurements in the visible spectrum.

articleTitle: Observation of terahertz frequency comb by time-window-extended, asynchronous-optical-sampling THz-TDS
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We observed detailed spectrum of THz frequency comb by extending the measured time window of the pulsed THz electric field up to ten pulse periods with asynchronous-optical-sampling THz-TDS (ASOPS-THz-TDS). Observed spectrum of THz comb mode has a linewidth of 5.6 MHz and a frequency interval of 56 MHz.

articleTitle: Square pipe-waveguide-based terahertz directional coupler
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present a terahertz (THz) leaky mode directional coupler for future THz applications. The directional coupler consisting of two square pipe waveguides works most efficiently in the minimal-attenuation wavelength regime.

articleTitle: 3D millimeter wave imaging of XVIIIth dynasty Egyptian sealed pottery
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A monochromatic millimeter wave imaging system coupled with an infrared temperature sensor has been used to investigate historic objects preserved at the museum of Aquitaine. Especially, 2D and 3D analysis have been performed in order to reveal the internal structure of a nearly 3500 years old sealed Egyptian jar.

articleTitle: Simulation of metallic nanostructures for emission of THz radiation using the lateral photo-Dember effect
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A 2D simulation for the lateral photo-Dember effect is used to calculate the THz emission of metallic nanostructures due to diffusion currents in order to realize a series of THz emitters.

articleTitle: Scanning laser terahertz imaging system using a 1.56 μm femtosecond fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We have developed a scanning laser terahertz imaging system with 1.56 μm femtosecond fiber laser for high-speed and high resolution measurement. Using this system, we succeeded in obtaining high-resolution THz images of various samples. An imaging speed of about 47 seconds/image for 512 × 512 pixels and a spatial resolution of up to 56 μm were achieved.

articleTitle: Infrared and terahertz nanoscopy for dielectric imaging and near-field mapping of antennas and transmission-lines
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We demonstrate nanoscale resolved IR and THz imaging and spectroscopy by recording the elastically scattered light from the tip of an atomic force microscope tip. Applications such as electronic and photonic device characterization will be presented.

articleTitle: Ultrabroadband coherent electric field generation from far infrared to 200 THz using air plasma induced by sub 10 fs pulses
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Focusing an intense sub 10 fs pulse together with its second harmonics in air, we have generated ultrabroadband coherent infrared wave ranging from far infrared to over 200 THz. Measurement with time domain spectroscopy assures that the wave is coherent. The mid infrared to near infrared component is observed with an HgCdTe detector.

articleTitle: Dielectric measurements and characterization of impurities of photovoltaic cell materials at millimeter and THz waves
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Transmittance, Refractive Index, Absorption coefficient, Real and Imaginary part of complex dielectric permittivity data for several Silicon, Silicon Carbide, Gallium Arsenide, Cadmium Telluride and Copper Indium Selenide specimens were measured using Dispersive Fourier Transform Spectroscopy and Free Space Quasi-optical Spectrometer powered by several Backward Wave Oscillators for the characterization of photovoltaic cell materials at Millimeter and THz Waves. Precision measurements easily identifies impurities present in these materials. Data for several silicon carbide (SiC) specimens and powdered Cadmium Telluride specimen over a broad millimeter wave range are shown.

articleTitle: An expanded view electron cyclotron emission imaging (ECEI) diagnostic
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Electron cyclotron emission imaging (ECEI) collects radiation from a tokamak plasma in a 1-D array to generate 2-D electron temperature images. Results are reported of new technology that doubles the horizontal coverage by increasing to 16 the number of simultaneously sampled frequency channels.

articleTitle: Database of all THz signatures measured on solids and liquids in the range 100 GHz to 10 THz
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A catalog of resonant absorption signatures measured on solids and liquids, by transmission and reflection, in the range of 100 GHz to 10 THz, has become a necessity for researchers in the THz field. In this work a THz database has been complied with 205 signatures of various chemical and biological materials. The database includes all published characteristic of the materials such as sample preparation, signature center frequency, signature frequency width, absorbance and attenuation coefficient at frequency center, complex refractive index (where provided), and the measurement techniques used. This is the first database of its kind and has the largest collection of THz signatures that has ever been recorded. All the signatures reported are experimental, and is conveniently accessed using a GUI-based search engine running in MATLAB.

articleTitle: Ghost modes in Terahertz Quantum Cascade Laser waveguides
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Degeneration of the lasing mode in a Terahertz Quantum Cascade Laser due to interaction with parasitic ghost modes is demonstrated here through rigorous numerical analysis. We show that such interactions can adversely affect the performance of a QCL by causing abrupt rises in lasing threshold. We also show that such affects can be avoided by altering the width of the metal cladding layer.

articleTitle: Magneto optical polarization measurements using THz polarization modulation spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report a new broad band technique for rapidly measuring the complex Faraday and Kerr rotations in materials such as topological insulators and graphene, combining the distinct advantages of THz time domain spectroscopy and polarization modulation techniques. The performance of the system is demonstrated using GaAs two dimensional electron gas in a magnetic field.

articleTitle: Terahertz time-domain magneto-optics using pulsed magnetic fields
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Terahertz time-domain magneto-optics using pulsed magnetic fields is demonstrated with two different approaches. The first uses a fiber coupled high-speed delay line in combination with a long duration pulsed magnet. The second uses a table-top short duration pulsed magnet scanned repetitively and a step-scan readout of the THz electric field.

articleTitle: Measurement of multiple parameters with Time Domain Terahertz in the industrial environment
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The nature of Time-Domain Terahertz data allows the simultaneous measurement of multiple product parameters. Examples include basis weight, coat weight, physical thickness, density, moisture, and multiple layer thicknesses. The capability of THz sensors to operate in challenging environmental condition makes the technology attractive for industrial measurements.

articleTitle: Origin of the terahertz absorption peak in single-walled carbon nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Two models for the universally-observed terahertz absorption peak in carbon nanotubes are tested experimentally with infrared and terahertz spectroscopy. The curvature-induced gap theory is disproved by our observation, while plasma resonance theory is partially supported.

articleTitle: A new feature extraction method in low-SNR for MMW radiometer based on wavelet transform modulus maxima
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In this paper, a new method based on the wavelet transform modulus maxima is proposed for extracting target features from the low-SNR output signal of the MMW radiometer. The experimental results show that the method can accurately extract the target's information of location and size.

articleTitle: Characterising Zinc Telluride wafers using continuous-wave terahertz spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Using a two-colour, continuous-wave terahertz (THz) source, we present a non-contact, non-destructive method for characterising the crystal parameters of Zinc Telluride (ZnTe) wafers. The high and low frequency dielectric constants and plasma and phonon frequencies of ZnTe wafers of differing thickness are found by fitting a simple model to the transmittance as a function of frequency. The dielectric function used in the fitting function invokes phonon, plasma and atomic contributions, which have not been considered simultaneously in previous work. The continuous-wave THz source allows for higher resolution at lower frequencies than is achievable with conventional pulsed-wave techniques.

articleTitle: Spectral and polarization characteristics of terahertz radiation from metaatom-loaded photoconductive antennas
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Spectral and polarization characteristics of terahertz waves radiated from metaatom-loaded photoconductive antennas strongly depend on shape, direction, and position of metaatoms. These characteristics are interpreted based on the symmetry and induced electric dipole of photoconductive antennas.

articleTitle: Dual frequency Brillouin fiber laser and 1.55 μm photomixer for highly coherent THz wave generation
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Using a dual frequency Brillouin fiber laser and a 1.55 μm photomixer, we report the generation of a highly coherent kilo-Hertz level sub-millimeter wave emission. This system does not require any electrical synthesizer, and low cost telecom components are used to achieve very simple source architecture. The THz photomixer is composed of a uni-travelling carrier photodiode integrated with an antenna. A ~ 1 kHz linewidth emission at 316 GHz is observed, with a signal to noise ratio >; 65 dB.

articleTitle: Evaluation of organic crystal DASC and DAST for THz difference frequency generation using a cr: Forsterite laser
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We examined a new type of organic nonlinear optical crystal, 4-dimethylamino-N-methyl-4-stilbazolium p-chlorobenzenesulfonate (DASC) as terahertz (THz) wave source via difference frequency generation (DFG), by comparing the THz-wave radiation from DAST crystal. We demonstrated the possibility that DASC crystal has some advantages as THz-DFG source in efficiency and damage threshold.

articleTitle: Terahertz emission induced by electron Bloch oscillations in SiC natural superlattice
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report on efficient terahertz electroluminescence from SiC structures with the natural superlattice. The emission spectrum demonstrates a single line, the maximum of which shifts linearly with increase in bias field. We attribute this emission to steady-state Bloch oscillations of electrons in SiC natural superlattice.

articleTitle: Using THz-TDS of ethyl lactate/water mixtures to gain insight into solvent dynamics
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In this work, terahertz spectroscopy was used to study the hydrogen bonding behaviour in mixtures of ethyl lactate and water. The results obtained show a marked deviation from a two-phase system, which agrees with data from other techniques.

articleTitle: Optical detected quantum oscillation with millimeter waves
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Cyclotron resonance was studied in quantum Hall systems of II-VI compounds with a vector network analyzer at a wide range of the millimeter wave frequency. We also observed quantum oscillation in the magneto-transmission at higher magnetic fields beyond the resonant field.

articleTitle: Towards sub ppq detection and monitoring capabilities for environmental applications using novel THz technologies
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Design and testing of a THz sensor ultimately to be capable of operating from 0.068 to 8.1 THz are presented. Results for modular approaches in the mm and submm spectral regions are reported utilizing cavity-enhanced techniques. Investigations indicate ppq levels of detection for molecular species with 1.0 Debyes dipole moment.

articleTitle: Broadband terahertz polarization optics using the giant Faraday effect in n-type InSb
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report on a giant Faraday effect in n-InSb probed via polarization-resolved THz time-domain spectroscopy. Rotation angles and ellipticities as large as π and 1, respectively, were observed in a wide frequency range, making n-InSb a promising material for broadband THz polarization optics.

articleTitle: Polarization and angle independent high Q-factor THz metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We propose polarization and angle insensitive metasurfaces for THz frequencies. The new unit cell consists of two concentric ring resonators with interdigitated fingers. The number of these fingers allows for controlling the sharpness of the bandstop resonance. A quality factor of more than 16 is observed. The experimental results are in very good agreement with the simulations.

articleTitle: Development of a matching optics unit (MOU) for the coaxial ITER gyrotron at KIT
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Closed corrugated waveguide transmission lines operating in the HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode will be used to transmit the powerful radiation from the coaxial-cavity gyrotrons to the ITER tokamak for Electron Cyclotron Resonance Heating (ECRH) and Current Drive (CD). A Match Optics Unit (MOU) has been developed to transform the gyrotron output into a Gaussian mode distribution with optimal parameters to maximize the coupling efficiency of the TEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">00</sub> Gaussian distribution to the HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode of the corrugated waveguide. The calculation results reveal that the coupling efficiency of the Gaussian-mode like wave beam to the HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode is approximately 96.3%.

articleTitle: Terahertz coherent control of a quantum Hall system: Kohn's theorem in the coherent regime
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Coherent control of cyclotron resonance in a quantum Hall system is demonstrated using a sequence of THz pulses. There is no signature of electron-electron interactions, generalizing Kohn's theorem to the level of coherent dynamics.

articleTitle: THz near-field microscopy applications in device research
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: THz near-field microscopy can make a large impact on development of THz technology. Sub-wavelength spatial resolution and the possibility of time-domain analysis make this method particularly useful in research on THz devices. Applications for device research, including mode analysis in waveguides and surface plasmon wave mapping will be discussed.

articleTitle: THz beam steering using femtosecond laser interference technique
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present a THz beam steering method that is based on the generation of grating lobe(GL) radiation from linear array antenna and interference principle of femtosecond laser beam. THz GL radiation with the bandwidth of 110GHz was generated from a strip-line photoconductive antenna. As the pump beam two femtosecond laser beams were combined with finite angle and produced an interference pattern. We demonstrated that the THz GL radiation can be steered by adjusting the relative incidence angle between two pump beams. The direction of the THz beam was changed by 20 degrees when the incidence angle of one pump beam was only varied by 0.1 degrees.

articleTitle: Strain induced conductivity change of SrRuO3 thin films observed by terahertz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We observed characteristics of SrRuO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> thin films deposited on various substrates in order to observe strain effect of the films, especially by terahertz time-domain spectroscopy. We found that SrRuO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> thin films on DyScO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (110) substrates show highly anisotropy of DC and optical conductivities.

articleTitle: Thin film transmission lines using cyclic olefin copolymer
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Thin film microstrip lines and grounded coplanar waveguide using a cyclic-olefin copolymer as low loss thin film have been fabricated and characterized up to 220 GHz. Attenuation as low as 0.6 dB/mm around 220 GHz has been measured on grounded coplanar waveguide with a 22-μm-thick cyclic-olefin copolymer thin film.

articleTitle: Terahertz cross-correlation system with a combless spectrum
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present a novel technique to generate a continuous, broadband terahertz spectrum with non AR-coated laser diodes. The combination of two spectrally controlled diode lasers and the use of their combined output in a terahertz cross-correlation spectroscopy setup results in signals principally comparable to that of femtosecond pumped TDS systems.

articleTitle: Nanowire-based architectures for the detection of THz radiation
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Self-assembled nanowires represent a new interesting technology to be explored in order to increase the cutoff frequency of electronic THz detectors. They can be developed in field effect transistor (FET) and diode geometries exploiting non-linearities of either the transconductance or the current-voltage characteristic as detection mechanism.

articleTitle: Au/Al-metal bonding conditions for double metal waveguide on GaN based terahertz quantum cascade laser structure
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We investigated metal bonging conditions of Au/Al layers formed on a GaN/Sapphire and on a GaAs substrates for a double metal waveguide of a GaN based terahertz quantum cascade laser. We found that the best bonding condition of Au/Al layers was under a pressure of 100 kg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at 200°C.

articleTitle: A 26 to 40 GHz wideband feedback amplifier using 0.18 μm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A 4-stage, Ka-band amplifier employing frequency controlled feedback with parasitic cancellation is presented. A novel gain response superposition concept is adopted to achieve a predicted flat gain of 17.2 dB ±0.8 dB over the entire waveguide band using 0.18 μm CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Emitter and detector modules for a fiber-coupled terahertz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We demonstrated a fiber-coupled THz time-domain spectroscopy (TDS) system. A THz output power of 132 nW of the THz emitter in the system was measured by a Golay-cell. Water vapor dips in the free space were clearly observed by the THz detector in the system.

articleTitle: Terahertz time domain spectroscopy of vertical silicon nanowires
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The complex dielectric constants of vertically aligned silicon nanowires (SiNWs) are measured by using terahertz time domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS). The SiNWs are fabricated on a (100) silicon wafer by a metal-assisted chemical etching method. It is demonstrated that the absorption coefficient of the SiNWs is significantly larger than that of a bare silicon wafer at THz band.

articleTitle: High-precision THz spectrum analyzer based on an unstabilized frequency comb
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We perform high-precision frequency measurements in the THz spectral region using an unstabilized frequency comb, which acts as a transfer oscillator. To correct the beating signal resulting from the THz source and one comb line of the rectified optical comb for fluctuations of the laser repetition rate, a simple and flexible algorithm is used. By this, we achieve an accuracy of the measurement setup as high as 9·10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-14</sup> for a 100 GHz test source. This is an improvement of two orders of magnitude compared to previously reported precision measurements in this frequency range employing femtosecond lasers.

articleTitle: Mode profiling of THz fibers with dynamic aperture near-field imaging
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present terahertz near-field mode profiling of different polymer THz fibers. Images with a resolution below the THz wavelength show the fundamental mode profile and higher order modes appearing at higher frequencies.

articleTitle: Mid-infrared third harmonic generation in highly-aligned single-walled carbon nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Optical properties of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) have been extensively studied, and much basic knowledge has been accumulated on how light emission, scattering, and absorption occur in CNTs. However, their nonlinear optical properties remain largely unexplored. Here, we have observed third harmonic generation from highly-aligned CNTs on sapphire with linearly-polarized intense mid-infrared radiation. Through polarization-dependent experiments, we extracted the nonzero tensor elements of χ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(3)</sup>. The contribution of the weaker tensor elements to the overall χ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(3)</sup> signal has been calculated to be approximately 1/3 of that of the dominant χ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(3)</sup><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">zzzz</sub> component, which is consistent with theory and other measured values.

articleTitle: Status of the development of the terahertz camera
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We describe our effort in the development of a low cost, wide-band detector/camera for generation of spatially resolved images of radiation beams in a multispectral range of wavelengths, from infrared to terahertz. The detector (T-camera) utilizes a thermochromic liquid crystal (TLC) film as the sensitive element in a temperature controlled chamber in conjunction with a CCD detector array. The T-camera can be used as an informative imaging diagnostic for terahertz sources.

articleTitle: Terahertz spectroscopic properties of three-dimensional split-ring resonator arrays
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In this work, three-dimensional, stacked split ring resonator arrays exhibiting characteristics at Terahertz frequencies have been designed, simulated, and fabricated. The effects of the ring spatial dimensions on resonant absorption frequencies and relative absorption strength are investigated and reported.

articleTitle: THz optical coherence tomography based on quantum cascade lasers
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The interfaces of a dielectric sample are resolved at terahertz frequencies by swept-source optical coherence tomography. The source is a 12-element array of third order distributed feedback quantum cascade lasers operating over a frequency range of 2.08 to 2.4 THz, at peak power levels of 100 μW, at 48 K maintained by a compact cryocooler.

articleTitle: Simulation and fabrication of large area uncooled microbolometers for terahertz wave detection
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Large area microbolometer detectors are very attractive for applications where high sensitivity is required. This is particularly important for long wavelength spectroscopy in the far-infrared and sub-millimeter region. This paper presents current progress in the development of large area uncooled microbolometer FPAs at INO.

articleTitle: Composite metamaterial waveguides for THz sheet beam devices
publicationTitle: 2011 International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
